_meta.description: Physical button-deck map for the Goldclub EGM, captured from the live hardware loopback bus. Built for automated test-case implementation (driving/observing button events).
_meta.source: Read-only WinDivert sniff of localhost:30800 while each button was pressed once, in order. Raw capture: \\10.0.0.90\c$\Windows\Temp\wd\dump.txt

bus.alsoCarries: Dallas/iButton key events and keyboard input share this port (COM8 -> 30000 + COM*100 = 30800).

pressEvent.encoding: ASCII decimal digits followed by CRLF (0x0D 0x0A)

otherTraffic.polling: client->server keep-alive/queries: CN, HP, ID, BL; server answers with a 3-digit status (700,701,703,704,708,181,...).
otherTraffic.lampControl: client->server 'YI <code> <state>' sets a button lamp on/off; server echoes <code>+499 (e.g. YI 271 1 -> 770). The YI 26x burst after a spin is the button-light chase, NOT a press.
otherTraffic.pressVsStatus: A genuine press is a bare button code (200-299 here) pushed by the server with no preceding YI request. Status/lamp-ack codes are 6xx/7xx.

bus.injectionNote: A press can be injected by writing '<code>\r\n' into the server->client stream on this connection (same mechanism as DallasSplice.exe uses for the Dallas ROM). Build-independent: this is the real hardware path the retail game consumes, not the debug 'p' hotkey.

buttons.name: Lines
buttons.note: DISABLED in this gamepack (confirmed by user). Input is not reported on the bus in normal play; an isolated re-capture produced no traffic. The single 269 seen in the full sweep was a transient armed-state event that also emitted an out-of-range burst (277,278,280,281,283,284,285,286,288,289,291,292). Treat 269 as the nominal Lines code but expect no events in this gamepack - skip it in test cases.
